ruling.recommended_action: Close the case as no_action: the sole off-route segment is exempt under RD-4(a) because a recorded LTA Accident on the bypassed Seletar Expressway stretch (reported 17:16, before the 17:38 detour) supplies the reasonable cause; no refund and no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so any unexempted off-route kilometre would flow into the fare through the distance component [F6][RD-2]. The GPS track shows exactly one off-route segment, 17:38–17:49, of 6.56 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, adding 4.92 km and straying up to 1911 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. No rider message names a stop or a road and no rider message agrees to any reroute: the only two chat messages are the rider's 17:23 arrival note and the driver's 17:24 ETA reply, both sent before the segment began [F7][F8][F9][RD-5], so RD-3 and RD-5 excuse nothing here.

The decisive question is RD-4(a): is there a traffic incident on the replaced optimal stretch, reported before the detour and within the matching radius? The record answers yes. F13 is an LTA DataMall Accident on Seletar Expressway (towards TPE) after Woodlands Avenue 12 Exit, reported 17:16 — before the 17:38 segment start — and located 0 m from the optimal route [F13][RD-4]. The execution trace confirms the code's own check: incident within 300 m of optimal km 7.1–8.7 [F3][F13][RD-4]. The driver's post-trip statement that an accident with blocked lanes forced the diversion matches that system record rather than contradicting it [F10][F13][RD-4].

The rider's attack rests on RD-4(b), and it is correct as far as it goes: the speed bands on record are Seletar Expressway band 5 (40–49 km/h) and Tampines Expressway band 4 (30–39 km/h), neither of which is band 1–2, so there is no severe-congestion corroboration and bands 1–2 cannot be inferred [F11][F12][RD-4]. But RD-4(b) is only corroboration; it cannot exempt a segment on its own, and its absence does not remove an exemption already established under RD-4(a) by F13 [F13][RD-4]. The event is dated and matched, the trace marks the RD-4(a) element ✓, and the fact table carries no record showing the Seletar Expressway incident had cleared before the driver reached it — F11's band 5 reading during 17:17–18:06 is not by itself a clearance finding at this clause level [F11][RD-4].

Because the single off-route segment is exempt, RD-1 yields no unexempted detour segment and the RD-2 amount is 4.92 km × $1.4099/km = $0.00 refundable; the billed excess line of $7.19 for 5.10 km in F4 is not itself an unexempted kilometre [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. The allowed outcomes on the trace are therefore no_action (or escalate), and nothing in the record shifts the metered fare: waiting $0.00, surge 1.0×, no post-trip manual add-ons, so FARE-1 is not engaged [F5][F6][FARE-1].

RD-6 does not attach. RD-6 requires the case to be established against the driver, which it is not, and in any event the driver's 90-day record shows 0 route disputes upheld, so the repeated-breach predicate is absent [F16][RD-6]. Profile facts are not used to decide the case in either direction [F15][F16][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The 17:38–17:49 off-route segment (4.92 km extra, up to 1911 m off the optimal route) is excused under RD-4(a): F13 records an LTA Accident on Seletar Expressway (towards TPE) after Woodlands Avenue 12 Exit, reported 17:16, before the segment start at 17:38, and located on the optimal route itself; the driver's statement F10 describes the same blocked stretch, and F11's band 5 (40–49 km/h) reading on that expressway during 17:17–18:06 is consistent with traffic still affected. RD-4(b) band 1–2 corroboration is absent, but it cannot exempt a segment on its own and its absence does not remove the RD-4(a) exemption.

Rejected in its conclusion: F13 satisfies RD-4(a) (incident on the optimal route, within 300 m, reported 17:16 before the 17:38 segment). Accepted that no rider message agrees to a route change [F7][F8][F9], but RD-5 consent is irrelevant once RD-4 reasonable cause is established; the driver's post-trip statement [F10] is read only as corroboration of the recorded incident [F13][RD-4].

Rejected: the refund computation under RD-2 requires an unexempted segment, and the sole segment in F3 is exempt under RD-4(a) [F13]. The $7.19 excess-distance line in F4 does not identify any unexempted kilometre.
Accepted as a factual point (waiting $0.00, surge 1.0× [F5][F6]) but it does not create a refund; with the segment exempt, RD-2 yields zero beyond the metered fare.

Rejected: RD-6 requires the case to be established against the driver and a prior upheld route dispute; the case is not established and F16 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so no flag_account attaches.
Accepted: F13 supplies the RD-4(a) reasonable cause for the segment, reported before the detour and on the optimal route.

Partly accepted: RD-4(a) is satisfied by F13, but F11's band 5 is not RD-4(b) corroboration (RD-4(b) requires band 1–2, under 19 km/h), so band 5 is not treated as supporting evidence — it is simply not disqualifying.
Accepted as to outcome: with the only segment exempt [F3][F13][RD-4], the RD-2 refund is 4.92 km × $1.4099/km = $0.00 and the metered fare [F6] stands.

Accepted: F10 does not contradict the system record on severity; F13 records the accident and a lane-2 warning, which is consistent with 'lanes blocked' enough to establish reasonable cause under RD-4(a).
Accepted: FARE-1 is not engaged — waiting $0.00, surge 1.0×, no unpublished or post-trip add-ons in F6 [F5][F6].
Accepted: reading the chat [F7][F8] and the driver's statement [F10] found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 are not engaged.
Accepted: RD-6 does not attach because the case is not established against the driver and F16 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days.
